content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To wean children off high sugar content cereals, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase decorative stickers for a "Healthy Choice" chart (15 minutes)
Step 2. Mix 10% low-sugar cereal into the current sugary brand (5 minutes)
Step 3. Introduce a completely sugar-free muesli brand (10 minutes)
Step 4. Research the glycemic index of popular breakfast grains (2 hours)
Step 5. Create a visual infographic of sugar content for the kids (1 hour)
Step 6. Conduct a family blind taste test of different milk alternatives (30 minutes)
Step 7. Buy a set of smaller cereal bowls to control portions (20 minutes)
Step 8. Print out a "sugar-free hero" progress tracker (10 minutes)
Step 9. Visit a local farmer's market to find fresh berry toppings (1 hour)
Step 10. Hide the remaining boxes of high-sugar cereals in a high cabinet (5 minutes)
Step 11. Read a book about childhood nutrition and habits (4 hours)
Step 12. Transition to 100% whole grain oats (5 minutes)
Step 13. Audit the current pantry for hidden sugars (45 minutes)
Step 14. Set a firm rule: no dessert-style cereals on weekdays (10 minutes)
Step 15. Discuss the health benefits of fiber with the children (20 minutes)
Step 16. Experiment with adding cinnamon instead of sugar (5 minutes)
Step 17. Subscribe to a healthy recipe newsletter (5 minutes)
Step 18. Prepare a batch of homemade low-sugar granola (1 hour)
Step 19. Freeze Greek yogurt drops as cereal "clusters" (3 hours)
Step 20. Serve a breakfast of mostly fresh fruit and nuts (15 minutes)
Step 21. Consult with a pediatrician about sugar intake (30 minutes)
Step 22. Watch a documentary about the food industry (90 minutes)
Step 23. Clear out the bottom shelf of the pantry for healthy options (30 minutes)
Step 24. Identify the children's favorite natural flavors, like vanilla or cocoa (15 minutes)
Step 25. Inventory all the cereal boxes currently in the house (20 minutes)
Step 26. Buy unsweetened almond and soy milk (15 minutes)
Step 27. Practice making "overnight oats" recipes (30 minutes)
Step 28. Take a grocery store tour to find high-fiber alternatives (1 hour)
Step 29. Implement a "one sugary cereal per month" reward system (1 day)
Step 30. Remove all colorful, cartoon-branded packaging (15 minutes)
Step 31. Host a "build your own parfait" breakfast party (1 hour)
Step 32. Bookmark three healthy breakfast blogs (10 minutes)
Step 33. Set up a dedicated "topping station" with seeds and nuts (20 minutes)
Step 34. Dehydrate apple slices to add crunch to cereal (6 hours)
Step 35. Compare labels of "natural" vs "organic" cereals (30 minutes)
Step 36. Transition to 100% unsweetened puffed grains (5 minutes)
Step 37. Purchase a digital kitchen scale for measuring servings (15 minutes)
Step 38. Interview other parents about their weaning strategies (1 hour)
Step 39. Mix 50% low-sugar cereal with 50% sugary cereal (5 minutes)
Step 40. Buy airtight glass jars for bulk grain storage (30 minutes)
Step 41. Start a small kitchen herb garden for flavoring (1 week)
Step 42. Mix 90% low-sugar cereal with 10% sugary cereal (5 minutes)
Step 43. Calculate the cost savings of buying bulk grains (30 minutes)
Step 44. Attend a community workshop on sugar-free living (2 hours)
Step 45. Explain the "sugar crash" feeling to the children (15 minutes)
Step 46. Label the glass jars with the date of purchase (10 minutes)
Step 47. Create a weekly breakfast meal plan (45 minutes)
Step 48. Try steel-cut oats in a slow cooker (8 hours)
Step 49. Purchase a variety of raw nuts (20 minutes)
Step 50. Donate unopened sugary cereal to a food bank (30 minutes)
Step 51. Remove the "cereal aisle" from the standard shopping route (10 minutes)
Step 52. Mix 75% low-sugar cereal with 25% sugary cereal (5 minutes)
Step 53. Mix 25% low-sugar cereal with 75% sugary cereal (5 minutes)
Step 54. Research natural sweeteners like monk fruit or stevia (1 hour)
Step 55. Celebrate one full week of sugar-free breakfasts (7 days)
Step 56. Introduce hot porridge as a winter alternative (15 minutes)
Step 57. Soak chia seeds for a pudding-like texture (4 hours)
Step 58. Read online reviews of healthy cereal brands (30 minutes)
Step 59. Establish a "Saturdays only" sugary cereal treat (1 week)
Step 60. Buy a bulk bag of organic quinoa (15 minutes)
Step 61. Bake a "breakfast loaf" with no added sugar (1 hour)
Step 62. Set a goal date for the total transition (5 minutes)
Step 63. Gradually reduce the amount of honey used as a topper (2 weeks)
Step 64. Buy plain, unsweetened cornflakes (15 minutes)
Step 65. Buy a recipe book dedicated to sugar-free breakfasts (20 minutes)
Step 66. Write down the family’s favorite healthy breakfast combinations (15 minutes)
Step 67. Ask the children to pick one "healthy" grain to try (20 minutes)
Step 68. Clean the pantry shelves thoroughly (1 hour)
Step 69. Transition to 100% bran flakes (5 minutes)
Step 70. Record the children's energy levels after a healthy breakfast (1 week)
Step 71. Look up the sugar content of "fruit-flavored" snacks (30 minutes)
Step 72. Toast raw sunflower seeds for extra flavor (15 minutes)
Step 73. Watch a video on how to make puffed rice at home (15 minutes)
Step 74. Mix 100% low-sugar cereal with fresh blueberries (5 minutes)
Step 75. Take a family photo to celebrate the health milestone (5 minutes)
Step 76. Blend dates to create a natural sweet paste (10 minutes)
Step 77. Purchase a new set of airtight "to-go" containers (20 minutes)
Step 78. Draft a list of "forbidden" high-fructose ingredients (30 minutes)
Step 79. Finalize the transition to zero-added-sugar breakfasts (1 day)
Step 80. Research the history of breakfast marketing (2 hours)
Step 81. Invite a nutritionist to speak at the school (1 month)
Step 82. Purchase a milk frother to make healthy "lattes" (15 minutes)
Step 83. Buy a kitchen timer to ensure slow, mindful eating (10 minutes)
Step 84. Set a monthly budget for healthy breakfast items (30 minutes)
Step 85. Learn how to sprout grains at home (3 days)
Step 86. Organize a neighborhood healthy breakfast swap (2 hours)
Step 87. Browse the health food aisle of a specialty grocer (1 hour)
Step 88. Mix 33% low-sugar cereal with 66% sugary cereal (5 minutes)
Step 89. Review the progress made over the last month (1 hour)
Step 90. Analyze the family's grocery receipts for sugar spend (1 hour)
